title: Causality and Kinematic Space
purpose: Build kinematic space from causal order and Lorentzian geometry, then connect its regional geometry to information-theoretic observables.
audience: Curious adults prepared to learn definitions and follow constructions; no presumed specialist credential.

competencies.statement: Represent causal comparability as a partial order without smuggling in metric distance.
Use light cones, timelike separation, and causal diamonds correctly.
Construct points or regions of kinematic space from intervals or geodesics.
Interpret geometry on a space whose points represent regions or intervals.
Relate geometric quantities to information or entropy without overstating the correspondence.
Work examples, locate failure cases, and distinguish established results from open questions.

assessmentLaw.completion: Every competency must be demonstrated in a resolvable exercise; watching or playlist membership is not completion.
assessmentLaw.negativeControl: At least one exercise must expose an invalid inference from causal order to metric distance.

successorRule: Material changes create a new revision that names this revision; admitted lesson products remain immutable evidence.

lessons.title: Causal entropy density in kinematic space
lessons.question: How does the local density of causal entropy in kinematic space relate to the curvature of the underlying spacetime?
lessons.whyItMayMatter: This connects the geometric structure of kinematic space to physical observables, providing a potential bridge between abstract causal order and measurable spacetime properties.

lessons.title: Causal structure entropy and spacetime reconstruction
lessons.question: How does the entropy of the causal order (defined via the number of distinct causal relations) constrain the reconstruction of the underlying Lorentzian metric?
lessons.whyItMayMatter: This connects the abstract partial order of causality to the geometric metric, addressing the core competency of distinguishing causal order from metric distance and exploring the limits of reconstructing spacetime geometry from causal data alone.

lessons.title: Causal sets and kinematic space embedding
lessons.question: How does the embedding of a causal set into a continuous Lorentzian manifold constrain the geometry of the resulting kinematic space?
lessons.whyItMayMatter: This connects discrete causal order to continuous kinematic geometry, addressing the competency of distinguishing causal order from metric distance and exploring the limits of reconstructing spacetime geometry from causal data alone.

lessons.title: Kinematic space and entanglement entropy
lessons.question: How does the geometry of kinematic space relate to the entanglement entropy of regions in a quantum field theory?
lessons.whyItMayMatter: This connects the geometric structure of kinematic space to information-theoretic observables, providing a potential bridge between abstract causal order and measurable quantum properties.

lessons.title: Modular flow and its representation in kinematic space
lessons.question: How can the modular flow associated with a causal diamond be encoded as a vector field on kinematic space, and what geometric features does it reveal about entanglement structure?
lessons.whyItMayMatter: Linking modular flow to a concrete geometric object in kinematic space could clarify how local quantum information propagates under causal constraints, offering a new bridge between algebraic quantum field theory and the emergent geometry of spacetime.

lessons.title: Causal witnesses and their geometric representation
lessons.question: Can operational causal witnesses be defined inside kinematic space to detect nontrivial causal influence between spacetime regions, and does the shape or curvature of their associated geometric loci encode information about the underlying Lorentzian geometry?
lessons.whyItMayMatter: Identifying causal witnesses in kinematic space would give a concrete tool for probing how information propagates in a relativistic setting, linking abstract causal order to measurable geometric signatures and potentially informing reconstruction algorithms for spacetime from limited causal data.
